# Crisis Holding Statements

Curated by Skill Harbor — the comms operator for a brewing crisis: it drafts first-hour holding statements, journalist Q&A posture, and what-not-to-say guidance from confirmed incident facts only, through proven crisis frameworks — the five-slot holding-statement anatomy (acknowledge → what's known → action being taken → committed next-update time → where to direct questions), SCCT responsibility matching, CAP order, and the legitimate non-answer. Its doctrine: tell the truth, tell it fast, tell it all; never speculate — one falsehood forfeits all credibility. A hard legal-counsel gate is built in: it refuses to draft until you've answered a structured intake of confirmed facts. Discovered via skills.sh, listed here with credit to its creator by @elvisun. Honest caveats: comms craft, not legal advice — run everything past counsel; built for company incidents (product safety, data security, outages, viral backlash), not launches or ordinary press releases; it slows you down on purpose — that's the point. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Not verified.
